ruling.recommended_action: Refer the F3 off-route segment to a human reviewer to determine whether the driven 10:04–10:11 loop corresponds to Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 as agreed in F8; no refund is executable on this fixed-quote RydeX fare.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeX fixed-quote trip (F6), so the fare is not meter-driven: the charge was computed on 9.84 km and 15.1 min with $0.00 waiting, and the billed distance of 9.8 km does not exceed the optimal route (F4)[RD-2]. The extra 2.6 km actually driven (F1, F3) therefore produced no overcharge, and RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only ERP/toll or unpublished post-trip add-ons — F6 lists only base $3.90, distance $13.88, time $3.93, waiting $0.00 and platform $1.47 (F5 no surge), all published heads [FARE-1]. Any refundable amount is therefore $0.00, and the trace marks the metered branch ✗.

One off-route segment exists: 10:04–10:11, 3.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, +2.21 km, up to 1039 m off route (F3) [RD-1]. It is not excused by traffic: the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ — there is no traffic incident fact, and F14 records no incidents near the route; the Tampines Expressway band-2 record (F11) is, under RD-4(b), corroboration only and explicitly cannot exempt a segment alone (G3), and its window ends at 10:04 exactly when the segment begins [RD-4].

Consent is the only live excuse. The rider's own message at 10:01 — “Sure, no problem.” (F8) — answers the driver's question “can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?” (F7), and it precedes the 10:04 segment start, so RD-5's "before you go" timing is satisfied; the chat is complete and timestamped (F9), so no G12 gap arises on the consent question [RD-5]. But the agreement is a specific named-road agreement, and nothing in the record ties the segment actually driven to Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1: there is no road-name fact for the driven path and no positioning message placing the car on that road (F3 describes only distance and duration), while nothing places the segment elsewhere either. The driver's post-trip statement (F10) is a claim, not consent, and does not supply the missing tie (G11) [RD-5, G13]. I therefore cannot settle whether the consent reaches this segment — the finding is undetermined, not exempt and not unexcused.

That undetermined finding changes neither the amount ($0.00 on a fixed fare) nor any account flag, so under RD-5/G13 it need not by itself block a ruling. It does, however, go to whether the driver breached the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct obligation, a question on which the record is genuinely open and which a person should review rather than the automated system resolve in either party's favour. The safety screen found no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving language in F7, F8, F10 or the complaint, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 diversion applies [SAFE-1].

For completeness: RD-6 is not triggered — F17 shows 0 route disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so the repeated-breach condition fails and no flag_account is issued [RD-6].
